title: How to Install an Electric Lantern | Copper Lantern Fabrication, Finishing, and Exterior Installation (New Orleans)

locations.name: New Orleans, Louisiana, USA
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly places events in New Orleans and references local context (e.g., Bourbon Street, New Orleans style fixtures).

summary: This Old House follows a New Orleans artisan and the project homeowner as they craft and install a New Orleans–style electric lantern. The episode covers: (1) the Bourbon Street lantern design tradition and what makes it distinctly New Orleans; (2) copper fabrication from raw copper sheets using a foot shear, a notcher, and hand snips to form decorative tops and panels; (3) riveted assembly as a durable alternative to solder in heat-prone lanterns; (4) an oxidation/aging process to achieve a 10–15 year patina finish; (5) final assembly including glass hurricane globe and electrical components; and (6) on-site exterior installation on a traditional New Orleans shotgun house, including upgrading to a proper junction box behind siding with weatherproof detailing and wiring that uses a licensed electrician. The video emphasizes craft technique, weatherproofing, and color choices (2700 K) to echo the historic gas-lit look.
topics: Foot shear and copper stock downsizing
Hand snips for fine decorative cuts
Riveting vs soldering for heat resistance
Glass hurricane globe and finishing station
Vinyl block with built-in junction box
Identifying hot vs neutral (ribbed vs smooth jacket)
2700 K soft white bulb for gas-like glow

sections.title: Shop tour: New Orleans style lanterns and the Bourbon Street fixture
sections.description: The host introduces New Orleans as the setting, highlights historic lanterns lining streets, and foregrounds the artisan's role in creating Bourbon Street–style lanterns, setting the environmental and stylistic basis for the project.

sections.title: Copper fabrication workflow
sections.description: Copper enters as raw sheets. The shop demonstrates cutting, breaking down sheets into parts, and forming decorative tops with hand tools while explaining material thickness choices and the mix of machine- and hand-work.

sections.title: Finish development: oxidation and final assembly
sections.description: Pieces are aged via an oxidation process to develop a long-lasting patina. The crew explains why rivets are used to secure joints (heat can degrade solder in gas-lit fixtures), and then moves toward final assembly, including sockets and the hurricane globe.

sections.title: Exterior installation planning on a New Orleans shotgun house
sections.description: Heath visits a traditional New Orleans shotgun house and discusses upgrading exterior fixtures, aligning with the house’s style, and the need for proper electrical upgrades while coordinating with a licensed electrician.

sections.title: Rough-in, waterproofing, and junction-box strategy
concepts: Vinyl block with built-in junction box
sections.description: The team introduces a vinyl-block solution with a built-in junction box to avoid cutting siding, then seals the install point to protect against water and pests, ensuring a flush exterior appearance.

sections.title: Wiring, grounding, and bulb choice
concepts: Hot vs neutral identification (ribbed vs smooth jacket)
sections.description: A licensed electrician guides the wiring process: bonding, grounding, and identifying hot/neutral on the fixture. The host selects a 2700 K bulb to achieve a warm, incandescent-like glow that resembles gas flame.

sections.title: Wrap-up and takeaway
sections.description: The completed lantern is shown in place, and the hosts summarize the craft, finish, and installation aspects, inviting viewers to subscribe for more projects.

featured_techniques.technique: Oxidation aging with pot ash and steel wool
